name: Jean-Claude Duvalier
summary: Duvalier defended a lifetime presidency and concentrated executive authority while periodically promising controlled political liberalization. His economic programme sought growth, infrastructure and foreign investment. His government suppressed independent critics; he continued defending detention for reasons of state after returning from exile.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He highlighted raising the daily minimum from one dollar to one dollar sixty as part of improving workers’ incomes.

strong-leader.rationale: He defended lifetime presidential authority as necessary for stability and economic reconstruction.

empower-police-military.rationale: He expressly defended creating the Léopards counter-guerrilla force to deter attacks on the regime.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His government protected import-substitution industries with tariffs and quotas, but by 1985 had committed to reducing protection.

one-party-rule.rationale: His rule excluded independent competition; the 1985 opening permitted parties only if they accepted his lifetime supremacy.

democracy-best.rationale: He later claimed to have introduced democracy while continuing to defend a record excluding competitive presidential succession.

separate-church-state.rationale: His revised concordat still required bishops and other senior clergy to swear constitutional loyalty before civil authorities.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He rejected presidential blame for violations while claiming legal and disciplinary intervention; that conflicts with the documented pattern of impunity.

separated-powers.rationale: The constitutional system he maintained put executive, legislative and judicial institutions under his effective control.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: His constitutional framework prohibited public-service strikes and permitted militarization during illegal or political general strikes.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He exercised unchecked emergency powers and prolonged decree authority suspending ordinary rights guarantees.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government crackdowns closed independent outlets and imprisoned or expelled journalists challenging presidential rule.

head-commands-forces.rationale: His personally exercised constitutional office combined supreme command of security forces with appointment of ministers.

death-penalty.rationale: He claimed in 2013 to have removed capital punishment, but his 1983 constitution retained it for treason.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He defended postponing electoral competition to preserve stability for solving economic and social problems.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He personally relinquished episcopal appointments in 1984, while retaining political consultation and clerical constitutional loyalty oaths.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: His system routinely suspended constitutional liberties rather than allowing them to bind presidential power.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He explicitly sought foreign investors and international assistance for infrastructure, reforestation and alternative fuels.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He publicly defended imprisoning and expelling dissidents as necessary to protect his government.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He defended inheriting power from his father as a means of preventing civil war and foreign occupation.

term-limits.rationale: He explicitly justified remaining president for life and called competitive presidential elections premature.

independent-unions.rationale: Independent labor organizers were among those systematically persecuted by his security apparatus.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1985 party law prohibited religiously affiliated parties and political meetings in places of worship.

notes: Reviewed his succession, presidency, 1977 full interview captions, 1983 Constitution and 1985 amendments, contemporary economic and human-rights assessments, 2011 interview and 2013 court testimony. Constitutional grants of powers that he exercised are distinguished from paper rights contradicted by practice. His own defense of lifetime rule, security forces and detention supports attribution beyond formal assent. General policy views are not inferred from his father’s writings or from the Duvalierist label. The 1977 video concerns the September prisoner release; its reposting page’s April dating is inconsistent and was not used. Reforestation claims do not establish beliefs about intrinsic nature, climate policy or environmental priority over liberty. Later democratic self-description and denials of abuses are recorded alongside the actual institutions and repeated public justifications. He died before a completed criminal trial; evidence of governmental conduct is not presented as a final conviction.
